rationale: The buyer is a specific, identifiable person — a solo developer or engineering lead at a company paying for Claude/OpenAI API access — and they demonstrably pay for developer tooling (API subscriptions, monitoring SaaS). Willingness to pay is real: Datadog, Better Uptime, and PagerDuty all command recurring fees for exactly this category of alerting, so the paid-substitute signal exists. The deciding factor holding this at 'validate' rather than 'build' is that the weighted total lands at 6.4, just below the 6.5 build threshold; one strong validation signal (even a 10-reply cold outreach batch with a couple of upgrade-intent responses) would push it over, so the next step is a small probe before committing build resources.
solution_plan: WHAT: A lightweight SaaS that independently probes the Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, and Mistral APIs every 60–90 seconds and pushes instant Slack/webhook/email alerts when a probe fails — faster and more reliable than the providers' own status pages. BUILD: The factory builds a scheduled Claude-driven probe loop (or simple HTTP pinger) that checks each API endpoint, writes results to a SQLite log, and triggers an alert via a pre-configured Slack webhook or email when failure thresholds are met; a minimal landing page (Carrd or similar) with a Stripe subscription link ($9–$19/mo) and an onboarding form collecting the user's preferred alert channel — zero coding required from Youval. SELL: Target developers complaining about AI API outages on HN, Reddit r/LocalLLaMA, and X/Twitter; the factory drafts outreach to a curated list of active HN commenters on outage threads (a public, high-intent list) and queues the messages for Youval's one-time approval before sending. MAINTAIN: New subscribers trigger an automated onboarding email, their alert endpoint is written to config, the probe loop runs continuously, billing renews via Stripe — Youval's only recurring touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing any support escalations the factory flags as ambiguous. CAVEAT: The core probe logic is simple, but standing out against free alternatives (UptimeRobot, isitdownrightnow) requires a strong 'AI-API-specific with faster alerts' narrative — validate that paying developers will pay $9+/mo before investing in full build.
notes: Build gates all pass: operational_autonomy=8 (≥7), buildability_with_ai=7 (≥6), buyer_clarity=8 (≥6), willingness_to_pay=6 (≥5). Stage is 'validate' solely because weighted_total 6.4 is just below the 6.5 build threshold — a small validation round (cold outreach or a waitlist landing page) is the right next step.
